messages:
Alex Chen: Handoff — quick summary: CPU pressure on inference-gw in us-west-2 triggered paging earlier. IncidentBot posted page at <https://redwood.incidents/1956789012>. Primary was Maya; Jordan is secondary. No PII exposed; customers seeing increased tail latency on /v1/generate (~+600ms).

Maya Patel: TL;DR we mitigated with a temporary scale-up of ded-queue and reverted a risky autoscaler change. Root cause looks like a regression in the autoscaler threshold math + a spike in batch size from a misrouted client. I left runbook links below.

IncidentBot: [pager] Severity: S2 — Increased latency on inference-gw-uswest2. Impact: degraded response times for hosted API customers (5% of requests > 1s). Trigger: 95p latency > 700ms for 10m. Notifying oncall.

Jordan Kim: Oncall notes: I paged in Riley for GPU pool checks. Primary/secondary shift confirmed for next 8h: Jordan (primary from handoff), Riley (secondary). I updated schedule in Opsbot.

Riley Gomez: Checked GPU pool health, all nodes report healthy but queue depth climbed to ~1200. Cleared backlog by temporarily bumping ded-queue to 20 workers, which drained in ~7m.

Alex Chen: Thanks. Action items for next shift: 1) follow up on autoscaler rollback PR, 2) add a safety cap to batch-size propagation in router, 3) create a short eval to replicate spike. I opened tickets.

Maya Patel: Tickets filed: INF-4321 (autoscaler regression rollback + tests), INF-4322 (router batch-size safety cap), INF-4323 (postmortem + eval harness). I attached short repro steps in INF-4323.

Jordan Kim: Runbook pointers for whoever picks this up: see /runbooks/inference/latency-spike.md — follow the "scale drain" section, step to roll back autoscaler is under "deploy fallbacks". Quick commands I used:
```
# bump ded queue workers
kubectl -n inference scale deploy ded-queue --replicas=20
# watch queue depth
k get pods -n inference -l app=ded-queue -o wide
```

Riley Gomez: Noted coverage gap: APM alerts for batch-size anomaly only run on prod-prod; staging wasn't alerting. Filed INF-4324 to add alert to staging and a synthetic test that pushes varied batch sizes.

Alex Chen: Retrospective scheduled: Thu 11:00 PDT in #eng-oncall-retros. I invited SRE, Runtime, and Product. Please add any pre-read notes to INF-4323.

Maya Patel: Follow-up for customer comms — support prepared a templated note for impacted customers, assigned to @support to send after final root cause. I put a draft in INF-4323.

Jordan Kim: Handoff checklist completed: primary signed on, secondary confirmed, action items triaged. I'm marking this thread as "handoff-complete" but keeping the thread open until INF-4323 PRs are merged.

OncallBot: Reminder: If you need more than 2h of handover, run a warm transfer and update #oncall-coverage with details.

Alex Chen: Final note — no further immediate customer impact. If anything spikes again, escalate to S1 and call the incident bridge. Good handoff, team. :thumbsup:
